commands.review_summary:
Adds a 30s default timeout to the Mattermost REST client and a loopback hanging-server regression test for timeout and caller-abort behavior.

PR surface: Source +25, Tests +145. Total +170 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. source-reproducible: current main routes Mattermost client requests through fetchWithSsrFGuard without a request timeout, and the PR body describes a real loopback HTTP server that accepts the request and never responds. I did not run the focused test in this read-only review.
commands.review_followup: - [P2] A narrow automated repair is plausible because the blocker is a concrete timeout-precedence regression in the PR branch.

target.title: fix(mattermost): add timeout to REST client requests
target.body:
Related: #95865

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Mattermost message delivery and lookup workflows could hang when the Mattermost REST API accepts a request but never sends a response.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared Mattermost REST client now applies a 30s default request timeout while preserving SSRF/private-network policy and caller abort signals. Existing Mattermost probe logic and DM per-attempt retry timeouts remain separate and unchanged.

## User Impact

Users and operators get a bounded Mattermost REST failure instead of a stuck send, reaction, upload, or target-resolution request when a self-hosted or remote server stalls after accepting the connection.

## Evidence

- `TMPDIR=/media/vdc/0668001470/tmp/openclaw-task-tmp node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/client.fetch-timeout.test.ts` - passed; `Test Files  1 passed (1)`, `Tests  2 passed (2)`.
- `TMPDIR=/media/vdc/0668001470/tmp/openclaw-task-tmp node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/client.ts extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/client.fetch-timeout.test.ts` - passed; exit 0.
- `git diff --check` - passed; exit 0.
- Mutation check: temporarily removing the guarded `timeoutMs` line made the focused Vitest fail with `Expected: "rejected"` and `Received: "pending"`; restoring the patch returned the test to green.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Mattermost REST client requests now have a deadline when the server accepts the request but never responds.

Real environment tested: local Linux Node source checkout; real `node:http` loopback server that accepts the connection and never responds, driving the real exported `createMattermostClient` plus `fetchMattermostMe` path.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: `TMPDIR=/media/vdc/0668001470/tmp/openclaw-task-tmp node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/client.fetch-timeout.test.ts`

Evidence after fix: the focused test asserts the loopback server receives `/api/v4/users/me`; without the timeout wiring the request stays pending past the race window, and with `timeoutMs: 50` it rejects with an abort/timeout-class error. A second test confirms a caller `AbortSignal` still aborts while a longer client timeout is configured.

Observed result after fix: `Test Files  1 passed (1)` and `Tests  2 passed (2)`.

What was not tested: a live Mattermost deployment; the hang is reproduced with a real local HTTP server, not the real third-party service.
